extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, third‑party requesters, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filings, petitions, comments, amendments, timing, and examiner actions in USPTO inter partes reexamination proceedings (MPEP guidance). Targets compliance with 37 CFR rules and MPEP handling to avoid expungement/denial and to understand consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit compliance (37 CFR 1.943) for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patent owner or third party submission must not exceed the page limits set by 37 CFR 1.943; oversize submissions are improper and will not be considered unless cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submission is too long, the Office issues a Notice giving 15 days to: (A) submit a redrafted paper within the page limit; or (B) file a copy with pages redacted to meet the limit. If no response, the improper submission will not be considered and related third party comments may be moot. See parallel procedure for third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pages excluded from the 1.943 page count
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain pages are excluded from the page limits of 37 CFR 1.943(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of contents pages, table of cases pages, pages of the claims (but not claim charts applying art to claims), and claims appendix are excluded. Sections of briefs required by 37 CFR 41.67(c)(1)(i)-(iv),(ix)-(xi) and 41.68(b)(1)(i)-(iv),(viii)-(xi) are excluded only if limited to the required information; if other information is included, the entire section's pages count. Exhibits/drawings are excluded unless they include arguments; affidavits/declarations that contain opinions/legal arguments are included in the page count; purely factual declarations (e.g., swearing behind a date, comparative test data) are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration content counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations containing opinion(s) or argument(s) about anticipation/obviousness or claim elements are treated as comments and counted against page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations limited to establishing facts (dates, comparative tests, data analysis) are excluded. Exhibits/drawings are not counted unless they themselves include argument; any pages containing argument are counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner single filing limit (37 CFR 1.951(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file only once under 37 CFR 1.951(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any second or supplemental submission by the patent owner after ACP will be expunged unless prosecution has been reopened. If paper is to be expunged and not accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183, the SPRS or CRU Director will expunge it; otherwise, OPLA decides the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester single-response limit (37 CFR 1.951(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester may respond only once and only after an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any original third party comments where the patent owner does not respond, or any second/supplemental responsive comments after ACP, are improper and will be expunged. Supplemental comments are limited to defined exceptions (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature filings are improper and expunged
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments or petitions filed at times not permitted by the rules (e.g., by a third party requester before the first Office action or before the patent owner has responded) are premature and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: third party comments after request but prior to first Office action (37 CFR 1.939); petitions to stay reexamination due to an interference filed prior to first Office action; submissions where the patent owner hasn't responded to an outstanding Office action (37 CFR 1.947). Petitions accompanied by 1.182/1.183 may be referred to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Too‑long third party submissions — cure options & timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party requester submission exceeds 37 CFR 1.943 page limits and is made prior to mailing of an ACP, it is improper but may be cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner issues a Notice giving 15 days to: (A) redraft to fit page limits, or (B) file a redacted copy to meet page limits. If no response, the submission will not be considered. See parallel patent owner rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party comments restricted to scope (37 CFR 1.947 and 1.951(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party comments must be limited to the scope provided by the regulations and to issues raised by the Office action or the patent owner’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments following the patent owner’s response to a first Office action must be limited to issues/points covered by that action or the patent owner’s response. Comments beyond permitted scope are improper and will be expunged; examiner action guidance at MPEP § 2666.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art submissions by third parties — limited purposes and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art submitted with third party comments must be limited to art necessary to rebut an examiner fact finding, to rebut the patent owner’s response, or art that became known to the requester after filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If art is submitted as newly known after filing, it must include a statement of when it became known/available and a discussion of pertinency of each reference to patentability of at least one claim. Prior art that does not satisfy these criteria is improper and will be expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental third party comments — generally improper, limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental third party comments are generally improper because 37 CFR 1.947 allows comments to be filed only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: supplemental comments permitted in response to the patent owner’s completion of a response (e.g., when initial third party comments were provided after an incomplete patent owner response) unless the patent owner's correcting submission is solely form and does not go to the merits; also permitted in response to a supplemental patent owner response. See MPEP for examples (e.g., purely form corrections like fee payments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party comments cannot respond to non‑Office‑action owner submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party comments are not permitted in response to a patent owner submission that does not respond to an Office action (e.g., a new power of attorney).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the third party requester does comment on such a submission, the comment will be expunged because 37 CFR 1.947 permits comments only in response to the patent owner’s response to an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition limitations and expungement (requester and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain petitions (e.g., to stay reexamination because of an interference, to merge reexaminations, or to deny extensions of time) filed at improper times or by improper parties will be expunged and not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: stay petitions filed before first Office action (37 CFR 1.939) or by a requester who is not a party to the interference; petitions to merge a reexamination with another reexamination or a reissue application (MPEP §§ 2686.01, 2686.03) are not considered if filed at wrong time. Oppositions to petitions have timing/entry-right consequences; OPLA should decide petitions where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions by third parties other than the requester — content limits (37 CFR 1.501/1.905)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions on behalf of third parties other than the third party requester will be considered only if they comply with 37 CFR 1.915 or are limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted papers: (1) 37 CFR 1.501 art citation limited to patents and printed publications with explanation of pertinency/applicability; or (2) bare notice of suits/other proceedings involving the patent (may include copies of decisions/court papers). Such submissions must be without additional comment, or they will be expunged/destroyed. Proper 1.501 submissions filed after the order to reexamine will be stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of service controls consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a paper is timely is determined by the date of service on the opposing party, not the actual date the Office receives the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent owner submission filed after the permitted time from date of service of a third party requester’s submission will be retained but not considered. Oppositions to petitions must generally be filed within two weeks of service; late oppositions remain in the record but need not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers denied consideration (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed unsigned, or signed by less than all patent owners where no attorney or agent of record is acting, will be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denied papers are retained in the file. Applies to both patent owner and third party requester filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proof of service may lead to denial (37 CFR 1.248)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that require proof of service but lack it may be denied consideration where service cannot be determined to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers should be denied where proof cannot be shown and other parties’ response periods are set by date of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective amendments retained but not considered; enlarging/new matter handled specially (37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments not complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k) will be retained in the file but not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the only defect is that the amendment enlarges the scope of the claims or introduces new matter, the amendment will be considered and a rejection will be made in the next Office action. New matter amendments to the disclosure must be canceled; claims with new matter rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112; drawing new matter ordinarily not entered. Amendment that enlarges claim scope will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature appeal retained but not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal filed before a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) has been issued is retained in the file but will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may inform parties that the appeal is not acceptable; cite 37 CFR 41.61 for third party analogous situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late papers retained but not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed after the period set by the Office for response will be retained in the file but not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to late filings by either patent owner or third party requester; example: third party comments submitted after 30 days from date of service of the patent owner’s response are retained but not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of art citations (37 CFR 1.902) in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Art citations submitted in inter partes reexamination are stored until the reexamination concludes and not immediately entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of art citations is permitted by patent owner and third party requester to the extent provided by 37 CFR 1.501 and 1.902; art filed after the date of the order to reexamine is stored until proceedings conclude (see MPEP § 2602).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival/acceptance of late responses petition requirements (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive an unintentionally abandoned reexamination prosecution or to accept an unintentionally delayed response must meet statutory and regulatory requirements under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable 1.137 petition must include: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)); (3) any terminal disclaimer and fee required; and (4) a statement that the entire delay from due date until filing was unintentional. Director may require additional information. Reconsideration of denied petitions must be filed within one month of mail date; extensions only under 37 CFR 1.956. Requests for reconsideration should include cover letter 'Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to timely respond (37 CFR 1.957(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, the reexamination prosecution may be terminated or limited depending on whether any claims are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no claims are allowable, prosecution terminated under 37 CFR 1.957(b) and certificate under 37 CFR 1.997 issued canceling all claims under reexamination. If at least one claim is allowable, proceeding continues but is limited to claims found allowable at time of failure (37 CFR 1.957(c)). Rejected claims terminated under 1.957(c) can be revived if delay was unintentional under 1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions after responses/comments — ACP, NIRC, or further Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: After reconsideration of patent owner response and third party comments, examiner must act promptly and has defined options for the next Office action depending on timeliness and substance of responses/comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely patent owner response: (1) if all claims rejected — issue Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) and cancel claims; (2) if at least one claim is allowable — issue Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) limiting prosecution to allowable claims. If timely patent owner response and no timely third party comments: examiner may issue incomplete-response action, Notice of Defective Paper in Reexam, ACP if proceeding ready, or new Office action if not ready. If both response and timely third party comments: examiner checks for improper comments or formality defects and then issues ACP (if ready) or a new Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration and conferencing prior to action
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of responses/comments, the examiner prepares for and participates in a conference (MPEP § 2671.03) and the proceeding is reviewed by SPRS/QAS before mailing action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must handle any requested corrections/revisions expeditiously and return to SPRS/QAS within set time. Patent owner and requester will be notified of claims rejected/allowable and may respond in accordance with MPEP §§ 2671/2672. Examiner will consider amendments for 35 U.S.C. 112 or claim broadening issues.
